title: [DECISION] memzero_explicit on ikm_buf ensures FIPS key zeroization before free
description: src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c lines 1923-1930 and 1969-1972: When ikm_fd \!= -1, ikm_buf is allocated, filled with key material extracted from the KEY fd, passed to the KDF provider, then immediately memzero_explicit'd regardless of KDF success/failure. The buffer is then kfree'd. This zeroization happens BEFORE the lock is released (line 1973). Comment at line 1923: 'FIPS 140-3: zeroize IKM regardless of KDF outcome'. Additionally, on error paths (line 1981-1983), ikm_buf is zeroized again in out_zero (pre-lock validation failure path). This double-zeroization (at line 1925 AND line 1982) is defensive: it ensures the buffer is cleared on all code paths, including early returns that never reach the main zeroization. The pattern is non-obvious: most code zeroizes once, but this code zeroizes both in the success path (within lock, before free) and in the early-exit error path (outside lock, for defense). This satisfies FIPS 140-3 compliance: key material must not persist after release.
